newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Horta delays speech to UN rights body amid row.
newsitem.headline: Horta delays speech to UN rights body amid row.

text.p: East Timorese independence leader Jose Ramos Horta has shelved plans to address the U.N. Commission on Human Rights on Thursday amid haggling over terms for his speech but says he hopes to do so later in its six-week annual session.
Horta, co-winner of the 1996 Nobel peace prize and a campaigner for self-determination on the disputed island, had been officially slated to speak on Thursday but withdrew at the last minute.

"Indonesia has mobilised some of its Asian friends to block the invitation to me...," Horta told journalists on Thursday. "We are ready to find a compromise solution so I can speak without a continued climate of confrontation with Indonesia."

Diplomats said negotiations were continuing between Horta, Indonesia, Portugal and the Czech chairman of the Commission to agree the terms under which Horta would address the 53-member body later in the session in Geneva.
They said points at issue included whether Horta should speak from the podium or from the floor.
Horta told reporters on Thursday he hoped the Commission would adopt a "strongly-worded resolution" on human rights abuses by Indonesia in East Timor.
"Torture is rampant in East Timor. Indonesia's military presence is increasing," he said, adding that there were some 1,000 East Timorese prisoners on the island.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 after Portugal withdrew from its former colony and annexed it the following year.

The international community does not recognise the annexation and talks under U.N. auspices between the foreign ministers of Portugal and Indonesia, aimed at finding an internationally acceptable solution, have dragged on since 1983.
